summary: SSE post-handshake silent tail with batched heartbeat causes partial final chunk and client EOF
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DocuSynth reports that long SSE streams intermittently terminate with the client receiving an EOF immediately after a short silent period that follows the handshake. The server later shows a batched heartbeat message emitted by the gateway and the final choice content appears in logs, but the client never receives the terminal delimiter.

Impact:
- Some generation requests for document summarization stop 2–8 seconds before the expected end, returning partial content.
- Customer says ~3% of streaming sessions in us-east time window 09:00–18:00 are affected.
- Symptoms cause downstream UI to show "incomplete result" and trigger a retry loop.

Environment:
- DocuSynth account on Dedicated cluster in prod-us-east.
- Affected model: redwood-1-large pinned v2026-02-28.
- Edge: customer routes through their NLB -> our streaming-gateway -> edge-proxy -> serving-runtime.

Observed behavior:
1) Client completes normal SSE handshake and starts receiving tokens.
2) After final choice is about to be sent, a 3–6s quiet period occurs (no chunks to client).
3) Client receives an EOF/connection-close without a "event: end" delimiter.
4) Server logs show a batched heartbeat emitted at the end of the quiet period and then the final choice entry in the serving-runtime logs, but no matching SSE end event to the socket send trace.

Expected behavior:
- Short quiet periods are acceptable, but the terminal choice must be sent and the SSE end marker must be delivered before connection close.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use customer SDK with keepalive=10s, send a long prompt (1200–2200 tokens output).
2) Reproduce on prod-us-east under normal load; issue surfaces intermittently.
3) Captured a failing session trace id: sess-ea4f7b2c.

Notes:
- Affected only for sessions that pass through a particular version of the customer's NLB (they confirmed two NLBs; one shows no failures).
- Client-side metrics show socket close reason as 1006 in some cases (abrupt close).
- No billing impact reported.
steps_to_reproduce: Client performs SSE handshake against streaming endpoint with keepalive=10s
Request large generation (expected >1000 tokens) with redwood-1-large pinned
Observe 2–8s quiet period near end of generation followed by immediate EOF without end event
Capture server-side trace (sess-ea4f7b2c) and gateway logs for comparison
logs: [2026-03-10T14:22:05Z] gateway[sess-ea4f7b2c] -> tokens streamed up to choice N-3
[2026-03-10T14:22:08Z] gateway[sess-ea4f7b2c] -> quiet window begins (no send operations)
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] serving-runtime[sess-ea4f7b2c] -> final-choice stored to log (choice_index: N)
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] edge-proxy -> socket closed by remote (client) code=1006
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Opened ticket, requested full packet capture and customer NLB config. Escalated to SRE.

2026-03-10 16:12 - Luis Romero (SRE): Replicated a quiet window locally when simulating the customer's NLB health-probe timeout behavior. Hypothesis: NLB TCP rebind + late ACK is causing our gateway's buffered heartbeat to coalesce with final payload, but a race closes the socket before SSE end is flushed.
2026-03-11 09:43 - DocuSynth (Customer): Provided a pcaps and confirmed affected NLB is Azure NLB with aggressive idle-timeout custom setting (20s). Also supplied SDK session id sess-ea4f7b2c.

2026-03-11 14:20 - Luis Romero (SRE): Instrumented gateway to emit socket-send traces and added a short flush after end-event in a canary build. Observed two reproduced failures with canary; end-event reached send-queue but kernel reported RST from client in one case.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Temporary mitigation shared with customer: enable client-side SSE keepalive and increase SDK reconnect window; awaiting customer confirmation on change rollout.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge NLB is performing a late TCP rebind/keepalive that interferes with timely ACK of the final SSE bytes, causing client to RST and our gateway to close before end-event is delivered.

Hypothesis 2: Gateway heartbeat coalescing optimization batches heartbeat and final choice into one kernel send; if the client closes mid-coalesced-send the SSE end event may never be observed by the client.
Evidence: pcap shows server FIN followed by client RST in 2 reproductions. Kernel send queue shows coalesced 14KB payload containing heartbeat + final chunk in traces where failure occurred.
Temporary test: added explicit flush and 50ms delay after end-event in canary. Reproduction rate dropped but not eliminated under heavy synthetic load.
mitigation_and_next_steps: Shared workaround with customer: increase SDK keepalive to 30s and enable explicit per-chunk flush option (available in the beta SDK).
SRE to open PR to make 'flush-after-end-event' default in gateway with conservative 50ms grace window and a config toggle. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-gateway/pull/5021
SRE and Edge teams to run load test with simulated NLB behavior to validate fix; target rollout to canary on 2026-03-14.
If fix reduces failures <0.1% in canary, schedule full rollout to prod-us-east with a 24-48 hour monitoring window.
resolution_summary: In progress: Provided workaround and deployed canary instrumentation. Code change drafted to flush after end-event; load testing pending. Customer accepted temporary SDK workaround and will monitor.
